notes: Sample webhost_config.json - the web console: how people sign in to it, and which components its dashboard draws. Copy to webhost_config.json and edit.

'web' holds the session and permission rules. 'session_days' is why closing the browser does not sign anyone out: the cookie and the stored session carry the same lifetime, so shortening it shortens both.

The 'min_level_*' values are checked against a person's level on the same 1-100 ladder telegram_users.json uses. view < edit < run < admin, and somebody needs at least the named level for that class of action. Raise min_level_run before letting the console reach a production instance.

'cookie_secure' must be true wherever the console is served over HTTPS, and is false here only because the sample assumes a plain HTTP address on a private network. Serving a session cookie over plain HTTP on a routed network hands out the session.
'max_failed_logins' and 'lockout_minutes' are the brute-force gate. They apply per account, so locking one account does not lock the console.

'apps' is one block per component - all fourteen. 'ord' is the number of its file under docs/, so the dashboard reads in the same order as the documentation, and 'app_command_ids' links a block to the entries in app_commands.json it owns, which is how a block shows its schedule and its last run. A block with none is a library or a CLI-only component and says so.

apps.summary: The database the toolkit keeps its own data in: job runs, metric results, reports, the delivery queue, and the configuration mirror.
One logger per app: files under logs/, rows in job_runs, and the notify level that decides which chat hears about it.
The scheduler. Reads app_commands.json and runs every other app on its own interval, forwarding the secret key to each child process.
Collects every metric from every enabled target and writes the results. Reports and SLA both read what it produces.
Runs the scheduled SQL scripts against their configured targets and delivers the output as text or a spreadsheet.
Turns collected metrics into the scheduled reports and the inventory pages the web host publishes.
Delivers the outgoing queue one message at a time, and executes the commands people send back.
Runs backups, proves them by restoring, and records what was verified and when.
Validates the objectives against collected metrics and reports the error budget left on each.
Provisions and moves the lab databases that drills and rehearsals run against.
Builds and deploys the toolkit to another node, and watches the toolkit itself - the only app that reports on the others.
Serves the reports over HTTP and hosts this console. Runs once and stays up rather than repeating on an interval.
The shared operations layer: run SQL, reach a host, move a file, rotate a password. Apps call it through its CLI, never by import.
Pure values and rules - time windows, notify routing, severity, formatting. Imported everywhere, runs nothing.
